html:
On 20 December 1999 Portugal handed Macau to the People's Republic of China, ending more than four centuries of Portuguese presence and the last European colony in Asia.

Portugal's grip had weakened long before. In riots in 1966, inspired by the Cultural Revolution, the colonial government gave way to local pro-Beijing groups. After Portugal's own revolution in 1974 it offered to give Macau back, but China preferred to wait. A Joint Declaration in 1987, on the model of the Hong Kong deal, set the date and the formula of one country, two systems.

Macau became a Special Administrative Region. Unlike Hong Kong, it passed its own security law in 2009 with little protest. Its economy came to rest on the casinos.
sum: On 20 December 1999 Portugal handed Macau to the People's Republic of China, ending more than four centuries of Portuguese presence and the last European colony in Asia.
